Fast C++ Implementation of p.GFisher Method="MR"

Source: R/RcppExports.R
p_GFisher_MR_cpp.Rd

Computes p-value using simulation-assisted moment ratio matching in C++. This function provides substantial speedup over the pure R implementation by vectorizing operations and avoiding apply() loops.

p_GFisher_MR_cpp(q, df, w, M, p_type = "two", nsim = 50000L, seed = 0L)

Arguments

q

Observed GFisher statistic

df

Vector of degrees of freedom

w

Vector of weights

M

Correlation matrix

p_type

String: "two" for two-sided, "one" for one-sided

nsim

Number of simulations (default 50000)

seed

Random seed (0 = no seed)

Value

P-value

Details

This function implements the simulation-based moment ratio (MR) method for calculating GFisher p-values under dependence. The algorithm:

  1. Generate null distribution: znull ~ N(0, M) using Cholesky decomposition

  2. Transform to p-values based on p_type (two-sided or one-sided)

  3. Apply chi-square transformations with specified degrees of freedom

  4. Compute weighted Fisher statistics: sum(w * pp_trans)

  5. Calculate first 4 moments from the null distribution

  6. Fit gamma distribution using moment matching

  7. Compute p-value from the gamma approximation

Performance: This C++ implementation is substantially faster than the R version due to:

  • Vectorized matrix operations via Armadillo

  • Elimination of apply() loops

  • Efficient memory layout

  • Optimized BLAS/LAPACK routines

Reproducibility: When the same seed is used, C++ and R versions produce identical results (within machine precision).

References

Zhang, H., & Wu, Z. (2023). The generalized Fisher's combination and accurate p-value calculation under dependence. Biometrics, 79(2), 1159-1172.
